situation: Rwanda, 1994 (Taba commune): Jean-Paul Akayesu convicted; the Chamber found that genocide was committed in Rwanda in 1994 against the Tutsi as a group
authority: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, Trial Chamber I
documentTitle: The Prosecutor versus Jean-Paul Akayesu, Case No. ICTR-96-4-T, Judgement
verification: Opened the judgement PDF on unictr.irmct.org (the ICTR archive kept by the UN International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals). Front page: Trial Chamber I, decision of 2 September 1998, Case No. ICTR-96-4-T. Section 8, Verdict: Count 1 'Guilty of Genocide'; Counts 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 14 guilty of crimes against humanity; Count 4 guilty of direct and public incitement to commit genocide. Para. 126: 'genocide was, indeed, committed in Rwanda in 1994 against the Tutsi as a group'. The case page unictr.irmct.org/en/cases/ictr-96-4 refused automated access (HTTP 403), so the appeal (2001) was not checked and is not entered.

verification: Opened the appeal judgement PDF on icty.org: Appeals Chamber, Case No. IT-98-33-A, 19 April 2004. situation: Srebrenica, July 1995: the Court found that the killings were genocide; Serbia did not commit it, but violated its obligations under the Genocide Convention to prevent it and to punish it
authority: International Court of Justice
documentTitle: Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro), Judgment of 26 February 2007
verification: Read the case page icj-cij.org/case/91 ('Overview of the case'): the Srebrenica killings 'were committed with the specific intent to destroy in part the group of Bosnian Muslims in that area'; the acts were not proved attributable to Serbia; Serbia 'had violated its obligation contained in Article 1 of the Genocide Convention to prevent' the Srebrenica genocide and 'had violated its obligation to punish the perpetrators of genocide'. The judgment's PDF URL is as listed on that page; the PDF itself could not be opened (icj-cij.org serves PDFs behind a bot check).

situation: Croatia, 1991–1995: Croatia's claim against Serbia and Serbia's counter-claim (about Operation Storm, 1995) were both rejected. The Court found acts that were the physical element of genocide, but not the intent to destroy the group, so genocide was not proved
authority: International Court of Justice
group: Croats (Croatia's claim); the Serbs of Croatia (Serbia's counter-claim)
documentTitle: Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Croatia v. Serbia), Judgment of 3 February 2015
verification: Read the case page icj-cij.org/case/118 ('Overview of the case'): acts against Croats 'constituted the actus reus of genocide within the meaning of Article II (a) and (b)', but 'In the absence of evidence of the required intent, the Court found that Croatia had not proved its allegations'; Serbia's counter-claim: the acts 'had not been committed on a scale such that they could only point to the existence of a genocidal intent', and 'it rejected Serbia's counter-claim in its entirety'. Press release 2015/4, 'The Court rejects Croatia's claim and Serbia's counter-claim'. Entered as a court judgment with outcome NotEstablished, so the app labels it 'Court judgment: genocide not established', never draws it on the map, and never counts it as a crisis. The judgment's PDF URL is as listed on the case page (the PDF itself is behind icj-cij.org's bot check).

situation: Democratic Kampuchea, 17 April 1975 to 6 January 1979: Nuon Chea and Khieu Samphan convicted (Case 002/02); genocide of the Vietnamese (both) and of the Cham (Nuon Chea, as a superior)
